answer:
Context relevance asks whether retrieved passages help answer the query. Groundedness asks whether claims in the answer are supported by those passages. Answer relevance asks whether the response actually addresses the question. A response can pass one and fail another: faithfully repeating an irrelevant passage is grounded but unhelpful. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217)

Build examples with known relevant evidence, independently check claims against cited spans, and score answer completeness and correctness. Include abstention when evidence is missing. Use retrieval metrics such as recall@k only when relevance labels exist; reference-free LLM scores are noisy proxies, not ground truth.

Separate retrieval failures from generation failures by rerunning generation with gold context. Calibrate automated graders on human-reviewed slices, track judge agreement, and version prompts, evidence, and models so regression comparisons are meaningful. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685)
